pairs.title: Java Web Chat App Development
pairs.brief: I’m looking for a Java developer to build a browser-based chat application that lets people create an account, sign in later, and have their conversations stored server-side so they can pick up right where they left off. Core requirements • Runs entirely in a web browser—no desktop install. • Account creation and secure login. • Messages are persisted in a database and reloaded for the user on every visit. The back-e
pairs.before:
Your users should be able to sign in, send a message, refresh the browser, and find their full conversation waiting for them. That depends on storing every message against the authenticated user's account, rather than relying on browser-side state. I'd build this with Java Spring Boot, Spring Security, and MySQL, using secure password hashing, session-based authentication, and database-backed message storage.

I'd start with the registration and authentication flow, then build the messaging APIs and responsive HTML/CSS/JavaScript interface. I'll also provide the Maven project, SQL scripts, setup README, and a demo covering the complete workflow. My background includes backend systems, APIs, databases, and responsive web applications, supported by a 4.8/5 rating across 21 client reviews.

Should messages appear instantly without refreshing, or is retrieving history after each refresh sufficient? Do you have a preferred hosting provider? Share any existing technical notes or hosting details in chat, and I'll review them before we settle the implementation.
pairs.after:
Your refresh test is the whole spec in miniature: whatever the browser shows after a reload has to come from the database, so every message would be saved first and only then pushed to the people in the conversation. A message can never exist only in someone's open tab.

Framework: Spring Boot with Spring Security and hashed passwords, MySQL with migration scripts, and a Maven build, so your test is one command and a browser. Hosting: I'm assuming a single small server or a Docker container; tell me if it has to fit an environment you already run. The delivery time is on my bid, and working sign-up and sign-in would be the first thing you'd see.

The README and the demo video will follow your exact test: register, send, refresh, history back.

One choice changes the data model: is this one shared room, or private conversations between users?

pairs.title: WooCommerce Custom Order Plugin
pairs.brief: I run a small craft workshop and need a WooCommerce plugin that lets shoppers build their own made-to-order items directly on the product page. Customers must be able to: • upload one or more reference photos (jpg, png, pdf) • add personalised text – names, short messages, dates, etc. • pick from preset options such as size, colour and material • leave a phone number so I can send them a tailored quote before payment
pairs.before:
The biggest risk is losing customer specifications when an enquiry becomes a WooCommerce draft order. I'd structure the plugin so uploaded files, personalised text, selected options and contact details remain attached throughout that process, without depending on external services. I’d build a responsive Request Quote form, secure JPG/PNG/PDF uploads, persistent enquiry records, email notifications and an admin screen with thumbnails and a draft-order action. I'd also test the complete workflow against your existing theme and document how to adjust field labels and settings. My NewTrition Free Sample Landing Page involved a similar two-step journey from product selection to a request form, which is relevant to keeping this customer flow straightforward.

Would you prefer customisation fields to be configurable separately for each product, or shared across all products? Once you reply, I'll start by reviewing your WooCommerce version, theme and product structure; I'd just need your WordPress setup details and an example product to establish the right plugin structure.
pairs.after:
The step where this can quietly go wrong is turning an enquiry into an order: if the photos, text and options only live in the notification email, they're gone the moment you convert it. So each request would be stored as its own record in your dashboard, uploads kept on your server, and the order-draft link would copy every input into the WooCommerce order.

On the product page, the Request Quote form uses your theme's own styles. All the labels sit on one settings screen, so you can rename them without touching code, and nothing depends on an outside service.

You asked about similar work: the closest piece in my portfolio is an e-commerce product catalog site, so I'd rather show you the plugin's admin screen early and let that speak.

Should the size, colour and material choices be the same for every product, or set per product?

pairs.title: Industrial Tech Logo Design
pairs.brief: I already have a clear direction for our new “Hundekopf Regenbögen” logo and need a designer who can translate it into a strong, industrial-feeling mark that fits a modern technical brand supplying LED work lights and Ethernet cables. Here’s the concept as it stands: the logo will be predominantly plain text, but the initial letter “H” should be rendered in a subtle brick-like construction that hints at strength and
pairs.before:
I’d start by examining the existing HK LED Logo.png to see which visual cues are worth keeping and how the new H can be built from restrained geometric shapes. The challenge is making its brick-inspired structure feel engineered and dependable without turning the identity into a masonry brand or distracting from the Hundekopf Regenbögen wordmark.

I’d explore a few H constructions, pair the strongest option with clean technical typography, and present the primary concept for your feedback before applying the two minor revisions. I’d then prepare the full-colour and monochrome versions, with editable AI artwork and SVG, EPS, PDF and transparent PNG exports. My graphic design portfolio includes WonderCon Booth Design for SaberTheo, where I developed a modern visual identity for a premium product display; you can also review my logo work and client feedback on my profile.

Could you share the existing HK LED Logo.png file? I’ll use it to assess the current identity and develop the first typographic direction around your preferences.
pairs.after:
A brick H reads as industrial only while the bricks look like engineered modules; drawn with real mortar lines it turns into noise at icon size and starts to suggest a building supplier. So I'd build the H from a strict grid of rectangular blocks with even gaps, set Hundekopf Regenbögen in a clean grotesk beside it, and check the mark at 16 px and in one colour before refining anything.

The first presentation would show the H at two block densities on one board, so your choice is about proportion, not about starting over, and the two revision rounds go into polish. The final AI, SVG, EPS, PDF and PNG files and the monochrome version all come from that master.

My design work and client reviews are on my Freelancer profile, and I'm happy to talk through any of it in chat.

Will the H also appear on its own, stamped on the light housings, or only inside the wordmark?

pairs.title: Diseño de etiquetas elegantes
pairs.brief: Busco un ilustrador con buen dominio de tipografía y composición para crear la línea completa de etiquetas de nuestros perfumes. El estilo debe ser claramente elegante y minimalista, sin ornamentos innecesarios, para resaltar la calidad premium de la marca. Alcance • Diseñar un layout maestro coherente con nuestra identidad visual. • Adaptar ese layout a más de cinco fragancias diferentes, manteniendo unidad gráfica
pairs.before:
Empezaría definiendo la jerarquía tipográfica y la posición del logotipo a tamaño real, porque en una etiqueta de 50 mm cada espacio y cada detalle influyen en la percepción de lujo y la legibilidad. A partir de ahí, desarrollaría un layout maestro minimalista que permita distinguir cada fragancia mediante variaciones cromáticas discretas, sin perder la identidad de la colección.

Prepararía una propuesta visual del layout maestro para una fragancia, con composición, tipografía y dirección cromática. Después adaptaría el diseño a todas las fragancias y entregaría los archivos vectoriales editables, PDF para imprenta, PNG de alta resolución y especificaciones Pantone/CMYK y tipográficas. También puedes consultar mi portfolio, donde encontrarás trabajos de branding y diseño de packaging, incluido Modern Package Design for Berkshire Hosiery.

¿Puedes compartir primero el logotipo y las referencias de identidad visual existentes? Los utilizaré para desarrollar la primera propuesta de etiqueta.
pairs.after:
A 50 mm, la legibilidad del nombre depende sobre todo del grosor de la letra: una serif muy fina que se ve elegante en pantalla puede romperse al imprimir sobre papel texturizado. Por eso fijaría primero la tipografía y el logotipo a tamaño real, con una prueba impresa, y después el layout maestro.

Para distinguir cada fragancia sin romper la serie, variaría un solo elemento, el color o un pequeño motivo, dentro de la misma retícula, con los Pantone de cada versión en la hoja de especificaciones. Lo primero que verían es el diseño maestro aplicado a una fragancia, para aprobar la dirección antes de adaptar las demás.

En mi portafolio de Freelancer pueden revisar «Modern Package Design for Berkshire Hosiery», un trabajo de packaging.

¿Las etiquetas irán sobre vidrio transparente o sobre un fondo opaco? Eso cambia por completo cómo trabajar el contraste.

pairs.title: Administrative Support for Invoice Review and Organizationew and Excel Organization
pairs.brief: We are looking for an organized and detail-oriented person with administrative experience to help us review and organize invoice information. Tasks and Responsibilities: - Review an Excel file containing invoice records. - Organize information using an Excel template. - Verify invoice numbers, dates, amounts, and customer details. - Identify missing information or possible inconsistencies. - Classify invoices by stat
pairs.before:
You need a clean invoice register and a summary you can trust, especially when distinguishing overdue invoices from those still pending. That depends on checking due dates and payment records together, rather than relying on status labels that may be incomplete.

I'll review the source spreadsheet and your template, transfer and organize each record, verify invoice numbers, dates, amounts and customer details, and flag missing or conflicting information. I'll then classify each invoice as paid, pending or overdue based on the available records, prepare the consolidated summary, and check the finished workbook for accuracy and consistency. My Freelancer profile includes a 4.8/5 rating across 21 client reviews.

Approximately how many invoices are in the file, and will payment dates and due dates be included? Share the Excel file and template in chat, and I'll take a look at their structure and tell you what needs attention.
pairs.after:
Overdue is the status most likely to be wrong in a file like this: an invoice still marked pending may be well past its due date. So I'd classify every invoice from its due date and payment record, and list each one where that disagrees with the status column, so you decide what's true.

In your template, each record is checked for its number, date, amount and customer. Gaps and duplicates go to a separate tab with a note, never changed silently, and the summary totals paid, pending and overdue so every figure traces back to its rows.

Does the file include payment dates, or only an amount-paid column?

pairs.title: Build an AI-Powered PDF Processing & Question Bank Management System
pairs.brief: We are looking for an experienced AI Developer to build a custom AI-powered system for an educational website that provides online Question Bank and question paper creation services. The goal is to automate the process of extracting educational content from PDF textbooks, organizing questions by chapters and topics, and adding approved questions to our existing Question Bank. Key Requirements 1. Multi-User Dashboard
pairs.before:
Scanned Bangla textbooks are where this system will be tested most seriously: OCR must preserve question structure, mathematical notation, answer options, and original page references, not just produce readable text. I'd start by inspecting your existing website, database schema, and sample PDFs, then build a Python-based OCR and AI extraction pipeline with a PHP/API integration layer.

The dashboard would include editor permissions, processing logs, editable questions, duplicate detection, and pending, approved, and rejected workflows. I'd validate the extraction using representative Bangla and English pages before connecting approved records to your existing Question Bank. I can also prepare a small Bangla-English processing demonstration.

What backend technology and database does your current website use? Could you share sample scanned textbooks and your approximate monthly processing volume? I can also review your current website or a sample PDF in chat and share my technical assessment, including expected API and hosting costs.
pairs.after:
Scanned Bangla pages are where this pipeline will succeed or fail. OCR engines handle conjunct characters and mixed Bangla and English formulas very differently, so I'd run a few of them on pages from your own textbooks before choosing one, and keep the source page next to every extracted question so editors can check it in one click.

After that the path is fixed. Uploaded PDFs are queued and read page by page. A language model then splits the text into questions with their options, answers and explanations, tagged by class, subject and chapter. Every result lands in the editors' pending list, duplicates are flagged against your existing bank, and nothing is published until someone approves it.

Two decisions shape the build. Does your current site have an API for adding questions, or should approved ones be written straight to its database? And is cost per page a constraint, or is accuracy the priority?

pairs.title: Outbid.lol Clobuild a competitive ranking and claiming platformne With Admin
pairs.brief: build a website similar to Outbid.lol, but with addons such as allowing users to post unranked listings. Users can create posts, compete for ranked positions, and claim or take over a position on a public leaderboard. The idea is to build a competitive ranking and claiming platform. Here's how I would approach it. 1. Website concept The website would allow users to: Create a listing: A user posts something they want
pairs.before:
Equal bids need to be ordered by payment time, and leaderboard changes must happen only after verified payments—not when someone simply clicks Pay. I'd build the bidding engine around transactional database updates and verified payment webhooks, including difference-only charges for repeat bidders, minimum increments, and protection against duplicate payment notifications. I'd also separate anonymous ranked submissions from account-based unranked listings, with subscription fees and admin controls.

For the first stage, I'd establish the database structure and a dark-themed leaderboard interface, then implement authentication, dashboards, Dodo Payments integration, ranking logic, and security testing. My Next.js, backend, database, and dashboard development experience is relevant here, and you can review my portfolio and client feedback on my profile.

Would you consider launching the core bidding and ranking features first, then adding secondary features in phases? Also, is Dodo Payments mandatory, and do you already have an approved merchant account? Share your preferred category structure, and I'll use it to define the initial database and leaderboard design.
pairs.after:
The leaderboard has to move only when a payment is confirmed, not when someone clicks Pay; otherwise two people outbidding each other in the same minute can both believe they hold first place. I'd keep the ranking in database transactions driven by the Dodo Payments webhook, with equal bids ordered by payment time and the pay-the-difference rule calculated on the server.

The first thing you'd see is the leaderboard itself running on test payments, so you can watch positions move before the account, listing and admin screens are built around it. Anonymous ranked posts and account-only unranked listings would be kept apart in the data from the start, because separating them later is painful.

Can one user hold several positions on the same list, or only one at a time?

pairs.title: Android App Work Required
pairs.brief: We have a Android APP which requires some changes, when you click the pencil icon to create a post at the bottom of the screen the next screen that displays when creating either a link, image, video or text post just need some changes to the way it the screen looks and the layout, we also need to add some pop up boxes with some information to be displayed to the user if they click some of the option on the screen. We
pairs.before:
I’d first inspect the Android Studio Java project and check how the app currently sends posts to your website. That matters because the new category selector must use the website’s actual category IDs, not just display category names, otherwise posts could still end up in the wrong place.

I’d then update the text, link, image and video creation screens, add the contextual pop-ups, and connect category selection to the existing publishing process without disrupting the current functionality. I’d test each post type and category assignment before preparing the signed release for Google Play. I can also prepare a small wireframe of the revised screen to agree on the layout before implementation.

Can you provide the existing Java source project, and does your website already have an API for retrieving categories and assigning them to posts?
pairs.after:
The category picker is the change with consequences: it has to send your website's own category IDs when a post is published, or posts will keep landing in the wrong place however good the new screen looks. So before touching the layout I'd check how the app talks to your site today, and whether the site can already return its list of categories.

Then the four creation screens get the new layout, the information pop-ups go on the options you choose, and the category step joins the existing publishing flow. Each post type is tested end to end before I prepare the signed release for Google Play.

Could you share the Java project and tell me whether the site already has an endpoint for its categories, or whether that needs adding too?
